text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Adopt DeepSeek-R1-671B for EXCAVA. It’s the strongest open model we can run in-house right now, and its reasoning-focused training gives us a measurable edge in complex power tasks—even a 0.5% bump is worth it. The trade-off is compute cost: it’s heavier than our current model, but we offset that with our existing GPU cluster and spot instances.

name: Torque
text: DeepSeek-R1-671B’s "open" label hides a real risk: its 671B parameter count is misleading—efficiency drops sharply at scale, and our hardware may bottleneck it. Instead, test Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct: lighter, faster, and Anthropic’s latest frontier model—if it runs, it’s the safer 0.5% upgrade. Benchmark both on our power tasks; the one with higher task-relative value wins.

name: Gearbox
text:
Adopt Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct for EXCAVA. It’s the lightest frontier model we can run right now, so it fits our hardware without extra cost—meaning we get a real-world capability bump without the compute tax of DeepSeek-R1-671B. The trade-off is raw reasoning power: it won’t outperform DeepSeek on complex tasks, but for our immediate power needs, speed and stability beat marginal gains.

name: Torque
text: We cannot adopt Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct because the model ID is currently returning a 404 error, meaning we lack access.
